newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks charge to sharply higher close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks charge to sharply higher close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks posted their biggest point gain this year on Friday, charging to a sharply higher close as investors welcomed a decline in U.S. bond yields and a surge in Wall Street stocks overnight.

The Hang Seng Index surged 284.85 points, or 2.22 percent, to 13,131.41, bringing the week's gain to 347.34 points, or 2.71 percent. Turnover was HK$6.97 billion compared with HK$7.19 billion on Thursday.
"We have a double whammy -- a very strong bond market and a strong Wall Street," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities.
The U.S. long bond jumped 1-16/32 on Thursday to yield 6.59 percent while the Dow industrials posted their second-largest net gain ever, rising 126.87 points to 6,473.64.
Alex Wong, technical analyst at Dharmala Securities, said he expected bond prices to rise further, boding well for Hong Kong stocks in the near term.

"I think it looks like we will see further upside in the Hang Seng in the near term but indicators are still quite mixed. We still need confirmation that the medium-term uptrend has started again," he said.
Wong said the rally would have to be sustained for a few more days before technical indicators show positive signals.
"We have had trendline resistance at around 13,350, so at least I think we need to break above there," he said.
Friday's rise in the Hang Seng was the biggest since August 30, 1994, when the index gained 287.48 points.

Franklin Lam, director of research at HG Asia, said Hong Kong stocks were just rebounding from recent weakness, in line with a rebound on Wall Street. "Hong Kong has come back almost six percent from the peak of this year," he said.
The index hit an all-time high on November 28 at 13,744.30.
Lam said Hong Kong was likely to remain tied to U.S. markets in the near term. "It will be a puppet to Wall Street," he said.
Shares in Wheelock rose HK$0.85 to HK$21.50 and Wharf ended HK$1.10 higher at HK$38.60. Swire Pacific climbed HK$1.50 to HK$73.25 and Hutchison advanced HK$2.25 to HK$60.25.
Property stocks also surged. Cheung Kong rose HK$2.00 to HK$66.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties gained HK$1.75 to HK$93.75.
Henderson Land rose HK$2.25 to HK$74.00 and New World Development gained HK$1.50 to HK$48.70.
